name: Card Fraud & Dispute System
description: Card authorisation fraud flags, dispute cases and chargeback status. Vendor-neutral in this build — ESFCU's actual card fraud platform is an open follow-up. This is the source that currently sees a seven-account ring the core cannot.

name: ACH & Wire Monitoring
description: Outbound ACH and wire activity with velocity and beneficiary checks. Carries the push-payment transfers at the centre of the current campaign — the ones members authorise themselves.

name: Digital Banking Alerts
description: Login, device, payee-add and transfer alerts from the digital channel. The earliest place an impersonation scam becomes visible, because the device and payee change before the money moves.

name: Member-Services Fraud Reports
description: Member-reported fraud intake, including the downloadable Fraud Packet and calls to member services. ESFCU publishes both routes; this is the human signal that often arrives before the systems agree.

name: Fraud-Scoring Model
description: Transaction and account scoring across the book. Actively scores 88% of accounts in scope; the 11,240 unscored accounts are predominantly the Howard University division, which is why part of that book is effectively unmonitored.

name: BSA & AML Case Management
description: Investigation cases, SAR drafting and the filing clock. System of record for the nine open SAR cases and their deadlines, and the source of the exam-defensible trail behind each one.

name: Core Banking
description: Accounts, balances and posted transactions — the system every other fraud signal has to reconcile against. Shared with the CEO briefing, so both personas read the same core figures.

name: Governance & Lineage Layer
description: Feed freshness, fraud-model coverage, SAR deadlines and exam posture, plus the source-to-screen trace behind every figure. This is what turns a fraud number into one the CRO can defend to a BSA examiner.
